gutter_arrival.speaker: narrator
gutter_arrival.text: The top of the spine. Below it the Gutter: the crease where the pages meet, where every drop of the flood ran in the end and had nowhere left to go.

gutter_arrival.speaker: narrator
gutter_arrival.text: The Sogg was down there. It hadn't stayed to fight. It had gone down, the way water does, and left the way open behind it.

gutter_arrival.speaker: patch
gutter_arrival.text: ...Then I'll follow. I didn't, last time.

interlude_4.speaker: narrator
interlude_4.text: Two in the morning. Dad had fallen asleep at the table again, his head on his arm next to the book. Nell had come down for a glass of water and hadn't gone back up.

interlude_4.speaker: gran
interlude_4.text: Old women don't sleep, love. We just wait for the kettle.

interlude_4.speaker: nell
interlude_4.text: Look at the middle of it. It's worse. It's black right down the fold, and it's still wet. The fox's page is empty.

interlude_4.speaker: nell
interlude_4.text: Dad's going to wake up and try again and it won't work, and he'll keep trying anyway. And I keep telling him it's ruined.

interlude_4.speaker: gran
interlude_4.text: He will keep trying. So did your grandad. They don't do it because they think it'll come back the same.

interlude_4.speaker: gran
interlude_4.text: Mended isn't halfway back to new, Nell. It's its own thing. You can see where it went wrong. That's the point of it.

interlude_4.speaker: narrator
interlude_4.text: The hairdryer was where she'd left it, at the end of the table. The plug was already in the wall. She didn't remember doing that.

interlude_4.speaker: narrator
interlude_4.text: Nell switched it to warm, and held it low over the very middle of the book, where the pages met, and didn't move it for a long time.

interlude_4.speaker: nell
interlude_4.text: Okay, fox. I don't know if you're in there. Hang on anyway.

ending_table.speaker: narrator
ending_table.text: Morning. Grey light through the laundromat steam, across Gran's table. The hairdryer had been switched off and put back, and its cord wound round it, neatly, the way nobody in the house ever wound it.

ending_table.speaker: dad
ending_table.text: Nell? Did you... The middle's dry.

ending_table.speaker: nell
ending_table.text: Mostly. It's lumpy. The fold's gone brown.

ending_table.speaker: dad
ending_table.text: It's dry. I'd stopped thinking it would be.

ending_table.speaker: nell
ending_table.text: Dad, the fox. The bit of tape on him, the tail. It's come off. It's down in the fold, holding the rain cloud together. Like he put it there.

ending_table.speaker: dad
ending_table.text: Funny. I don't remember taping the cloud.

ending_table.speaker: nell
ending_table.text: He needs a new one, then. Hang on.

ending_table.speaker: narrator
ending_table.text: Nell cut a strip from the corner of the harbour map, the bit that had never quite dried flat, and folded it into a tail, and taped it on.

ending_table.speaker: dad
ending_table.text: Tape on the inside, so it doesn't show?

ending_table.speaker: nell
ending_table.text: And there's a blank page at the back. It's been blank since I was born.

ending_table.speaker: dad
ending_table.text: I never knew what to put there.

ending_table.speaker: nell
ending_table.text: I do. Pass me the crayons. And don't watch.

epilogue_arrival.speaker: patch
epilogue_arrival.text: This page is new. It smells of crayon.

epilogue_arrival.speaker: patch
epilogue_arrival.text: Someone made it. Out of a bit of the harbour map. It's taped on, and the tape's on the outside. On purpose.

epilogue_arrival.speaker: corrugate
epilogue_arrival.text: Suits you, fox. A tail with a map on it. You'll always know where you've been.

epilogue_arrival.speaker: patch
epilogue_arrival.text: ...That's the nicest thing you've ever said to me.

epilogue_arrival.speaker: corrugate
epilogue_arrival.text: I've had it ready since the snow. Didn't want to waste it.

epilogue_arrival.speaker: dot
epilogue_arrival.text: Everyone's here. Go and see them. Then: last page.

epilogue_drizzle.speaker: drizzle
epilogue_drizzle.text: Everyone keeps being kind to me. I don't know what to do with it.

epilogue_drizzle.speaker: drizzle
epilogue_drizzle.text: Shepherd Fluff asked if I'd rain on the meadow on Thursdays. Just a little. For the grass. Nobody's asked me for anything since the flood.

epilogue_drizzle.speaker: drizzle
epilogue_drizzle.text: ...You can see the stitches from right across the page. I checked.

epilogue_bindwell.speaker: bindwell
epilogue_bindwell.text: The spine's restrung. Kettle stitch, every signature, and a door in every page. I sewed the doors in first this time.

epilogue_bindwell.speaker: bindwell
epilogue_bindwell.text: You gave her the tape. Good. A mend you can see is an honest one. I should know. I sewed the dishonest kind for long enough.

epilogue_fluff.speaker: shepherd_fluff
epilogue_fluff.text: Well, look at you. A tail again.

epilogue_fluff.speaker: patch
epilogue_fluff.text: You can tell everyone the real story, by the way. The running away bit. I don't mind.

epilogue_fluff.speaker: shepherd_fluff
epilogue_fluff.text: Already did, lad. Years ago. Well. Two chapters ago. Nobody thought less of you.

epilogue_fluff.speaker: shepherd_fluff
epilogue_fluff.text: Sheep don't care about tails. We care who comes back for us. You did.

epilogue_lamplighters.speaker: lamplighters
epilogue_lamplighters.text: We're lighting the lanterns again tonight. All of them. On this page, because it's the only one that's properly dry.

epilogue_lamplighters.speaker: lamplighters
epilogue_lamplighters.text: Bring the cloud. Five lanterns for five sisters, and a little rain over them. It's how our mother used to do it.

the_end.speaker: narrator
the_end.text: On the last page of the book, under Dad's old handwriting, there was a new line, in crayon.

the_end.speaker: nell_hand
the_end.text: THE POP-UP KINGDOM OF FOLDWICK. Soaked, torn, dried, taped, and finished.

the_end.speaker: nell_hand
the_end.text: Made by Dad. Mended by Dad, Gran, and Nell. And a fox.

the_end_all_letters.speaker: narrator
the_end_all_letters.text: On the last page of the book, under Dad's old handwriting, there was a new line, in crayon.

the_end_all_letters.speaker: nell_hand
the_end_all_letters.text: THE POP-UP KINGDOM OF FOLDWICK. Soaked, torn, dried, taped, and finished.

the_end_all_letters.speaker: nell_hand
the_end_all_letters.text: Made by Dad. Mended by Dad, Gran, and Nell. And a fox.

the_end_all_letters.speaker: narrator
the_end_all_letters.text: And above it, where the flood had washed the page blank, every Lost Letter had found its way home. Letter by letter, an older line came back: the first thing Dad ever wrote in the book.

the_end_all_letters.speaker: dad_hand
the_end_all_letters.text: FOR NELL, ON THE DAY YOU WERE BORN.

the_end_all_letters.speaker: dad_hand
the_end_all_letters.text: Everything in here can be folded, and unfolded, and folded again. Nothing in here is ever really ruined. Neither are you.

sogg_tail.speaker: narrator
sogg_tail.text: Patch knelt down on the floor of the Gutter, in the last of the water, beside her.

sogg_tail.speaker: drizzle
sogg_tail.text: Don't. I'm ruined. Look at me. I went down into the ink and I turned into that, and I drowned the whole book to make it stop hurting.

sogg_tail.speaker: patch
sogg_tail.text: I know. I saw. I've been walking through it for weeks.

sogg_tail.speaker: drizzle
sogg_tail.text: You pulled away. I had your tail in both hands and you pulled.

sogg_tail.speaker: patch
sogg_tail.text: I did. And then I ran, and I didn't look back, and I told everyone it was a storm. There wasn't a storm. There was just me.

sogg_tail.speaker: narrator
sogg_tail.text: He reached round behind him, to the strip of tape the lamplighters had given him: the only tail he'd had since the night of the flood. It came away a stitch at a time.

sogg_tail.speaker: patch
sogg_tail.text: It was always the thing you were holding on to. You might as well have it.

sogg_tail.speaker: narrator
sogg_tail.text: Gran's shears weren't made for cutting. They were made for this. He threaded the tape through the eye of the stork's bill and sewed her up the middle, small stitches, the way Gran did, and tied it off.

sogg_tail.speaker: narrator
sogg_tail.text: Far above them, at the very edge of the page, the warm light was still on. It stayed on all night.
